requirements.title: The stdio probe performs initialize, notifications/initialized, then up to ten tools/list pages

Send the notifications/initialized notification. Return MCPProbeResult(serverName, serverVersion, tools). A server that keeps returning a cursor is cut off after the tenth page with the tools gathered so far.

Replies for other ids are discarded, not queued - unlike the in-app hub, which keeps them.

deadline -> "The server didn't answer in time."

requirements.title: A probed child is asked to stop and is killed a second later, by process group when it leads one
requirements.action: The probe finishes, fails or is cancelled, or a hub client stops.

Otherwise send the terminate signal, then one second later, if it is still running, kill it: the whole process group when getpgid(pid) == pid (the child leads its own group), otherwise the single pid. requirements.title: Probe stdout is split on newlines and stderr is capped at 64000 bytes, keeping the last 16000

A contentLength over 33554432 answers 413 with {"error":"request body too large"}. When the bytes already buffered reach contentLength, exactly that many are taken and the request is routed. Otherwise more are read; if the stream completes or errors early, whatever was received is routed AS THE BODY with no error at all, so a client that dies mid-upload has its truncated payload relayed upstream. requirements.title: The proxy forwards exactly five client headers, adds the route's headers and a fresh bearer token, and holds the upstream request for an hour

The upstream request uses the client's method verbatim (any method is relayed) and timeoutInterval 3600, so a streaming session survives an hour. Exactly five client headers are copied, in this order, lowercase name to canonical name: content-type to Content-Type, accept to Accept, mcp-session-id to Mcp-Session-Id, mcp-protocol-version to MCP-Protocol-Version, last-event-id to Last-Event-ID. Nothing else is forwarded: no cookies, no user agent, no client Authorization. The route's own headers are applied next. When the route uses OAuth, an access token is fetched and set as "Bearer <token>"; a failure there answers 401 with {"error":"<the error's localized description>"} and returns. A non-empty body is attached.

There is no forced-refresh path anywhere. This is upstream behavior and is reproduced.

requirements.title: An event-stream response is relayed as chunked transfer with one chunk per byte

Transfer-Encoding: chunked and Connection: close are appended to the copied headers and the status head is sent. Then, for every byte of the upstream stream, the three-part frame "1
" + that one byte + "
" is sent as its own awaited write - six bytes on the wire and one async round trip per payload byte. A stream error ends the loop silently. The terminating chunk "0

" is sent, then the connection is cancelled and forgotten. This is severely inefficient but correctness-preserving, and it is upstream behavior: reproduce it rather than batching, because timing-sensitive downstream behavior may depend on the flush per byte.

Content-Length with the buffer's byte count and Connection: close are appended, the status head and the buffer are sent as one write, and the connection is cancelled and forgotten. Unlike the SSE branch, a stream error here is NOT caught and propagates to the caller, which answers 502 {"error":"upstream request failed"} - on a connection whose response may already be partly written.

failure_cases: a mid-stream upstream error escapes and triggers the caller's 502 path
requirements.windows_path: Reproduce the buffering and the asymmetric error handling between the two branches.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture with a large body and one with a mid-stream failure

requirements.title: Discovery reads protected-resource metadata from the 401 challenge, or probes two well-known paths
requirements.expected_result: An unparseable address throws discoveryFailed("That address doesn't look like a URL."). A GET of the address with Accept: application/json and a 30-second timeout is made; only a 401 response is inspected, and every WWW-Authenticate header on it (matched case-insensitively, whether a single string or a list) is scanned for a resource_metadata parameter and a scope parameter, stopping once both are found. When a resource_metadata URL was found, it is fetched and authorization_servers[0], resource and scopes_supported are read from it. When it was NOT found, two candidates are tried in order: "<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource<path of the address>" then "<origin>/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource"; the first that parses AND has either an authorization_servers array or a resource string is used and the loop stops. scopes_supported becomes the scope list only when it yields at least one non-empty name. When no scopes were found that way, the scopes from the challenge are used. issuer defaults to the address's origin; it is trimmed of leading and trailing "/" characters and, if empty, throws discoveryFailed("That address doesn't look like a URL."). Only authorization_servers[0] is ever used; later entries are ignored.
side_effects: one GET of the MCP address plus up to three metadata GETs
failure_cases: a non-401 answer or a network failure simply yields no challenge and falls through to the two candidates
no usable metadata anywhere -> metadataFailed with the last error detail
requirements.cancellation: each request is a cancellation point
requirements.windows_path: Same order, same two candidates, same single-issuer rule, and accept a bare unquoted resource_metadata value.

Trim the remainder of leading whitespace. When it starts with a double quote, the value is everything up to the next double quote, and an unterminated quote yields nil. Otherwise the value is the leading run of characters that are neither a comma nor a space. An empty value yields nil. challengeScopes splits the scope parameter on single spaces, drops empty names, and yields nil when nothing remains.

requirements.windows_path: Same permissive parse; Stripe sends resource_metadata unquoted and would be lost by a strict RFC 9110 parser.

When the issuer parses and has a path that is neither empty nor "/", two candidates come first: "<origin>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server<path>" then "<origin>/.well-known/openid-configuration<path>". Then always: "<base>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server" and "<base>/.well-known/openid-configuration". Each is fetched in order; the first that parses and has a non-empty authorization_endpoint AND a non-empty token_endpoint wins and yields AuthServerMetadata(issuer: base, authorizationEndpoint, tokenEndpoint, registrationEndpoint: the registration_endpoint string or nil, resource, resourceScopes). A document missing either endpoint records the detail "It's missing the addresses needed to sign in." and the loop continues. Exhausting the candidates throws metadataFailed(lastError), where lastError is the detail from the LAST failure only.

requirements.title: The bridge connects each server with a 15-second cap, strictly one after another, and never kills a spawned child

requirements.title: The bridge speaks a deliberately different dialect from the two Swift clients
source_evidence: DroppyCode/Services/MCP/MCPBridgeSource.swift:138 and :203 the clientInfo with no version

An SSE frame is accepted when its data parses to an object having "result" OR "error" - not, as in the Swift clients, an "id" - and a data payload of "[DONE]" is skipped. A tool's description falls back to its own name when absent or empty, and its schema falls back to the literal {type: "object"} with no properties key. Result content maps a text item to its text and EVERY other item to the literal "[image]", joined with newlines; an isError result is returned as "Error: " plus that text or, when empty, "Error: tool failed"; a thrown error is returned as "Error: " plus its message rather than rejecting.

requirements.title: The bridge's stdio transport frames JSON lines, matches replies by id, and fails every pending call when the child dies

Writes are JSON plus a newline; a write error removes the pending entry and rejects. A child error event, or its exit, fails every pending call with {error: {message: <text>}} and rejects the connection once. The handshake is initialize, then the notifications/initialized notification with an empty params object, then tools/list paged until nextCursor is falsy, with an empty params object on the first page. Tools are then wrapped with a call function bound to tools/call.

failure_cases: "process exited" is the message when the child dies

requirements.title: The setup panel follows its own content height, keeping its top edge fixed
requirements.action: Its content grows or shrinks, for example when the status line appears or the success view replaces the steps.
requirements.expected_result: The reported content height is rounded up and floored at 100. When it differs from the panel's current height by more than one point, the panel's frame origin y is raised by the difference and the height is set, so the top edge stays where it is and the panel grows downward. Nothing happens when the panel is not visible.
failure_cases: none
requirements.windows_path: Same top-anchored resize. Note macOS y coordinates grow upward; on Windows the equivalent is keeping the top edge and extending the bottom.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test driving a failed re-check and asserting the top edge does not move

requirements.title: The setup panel shows the reason, the numbered steps, an open-page button and Check again, and reports what a failed re-check found
requirements.preconditions: The setup panel is open and the server is not connected.
requirements.action: The panel renders, and the user presses Check again.
requirements.expected_result: The reason line at 12 points in the primary text colour, then the guide's steps as numbered rows in order, then a row holding a button labelled with the guide's page label on the left and, on the right, either a spinner beside the word "Checking" while the state is connecting, or a prominent button reading "Check again". Pressing Check again records that a check happened and calls refresh. Pressing the page button reopens the guide page. Once a check has happened and the state is no longer connecting: a still-needsSetup state shows "Still off on the server's side. " concatenated with the guide's note, or with nothing when the guide has no note, in the warning colour; a failed state shows the failure message in the danger colour. Both wrap to as many lines as they need.
side_effects: Check again starts a probe; the page button opens a browser tab
failure_cases: the two status lines above
requirements.cancellation: the probe is cancellable by other actions
requirements.windows_path: Verbatim strings, including the trailing space inside "Still off on the server's side. " before the note.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test driving a failing re-check and a failing probe

requirements.title: When the server finally connects, the setup panel shows a success view and closes itself 1.2 seconds later
requirements.expected_result: The whole body is replaced by the success view: a filled check-mark circle glyph at 34 points in the success colour, scaled from 0.5 to 1 with a 0.5-second spring of bounce 0.4, or set straight to 1 when reduce-motion is on; below it the line "Connected · " plus the tool count plus " tools" at 12 points medium in the primary text colour, using a middle dot U+00B7 with a space on each side. The block is centred with a minimum height of 120. A task then waits 1.2 seconds and closes the panel.
side_effects: the panel resizes through fit(), then closes
failure_cases: none
requirements.cancellation: the 1.2-second task is not cancelled if the user closes the panel first
requirements.windows_path: Same delay, the same spring and the same middle-dot string. The count is read from the connected state, so a zero-tool server reads "Connected · 0 tools".
requirements.verification_method: interaction test asserting the panel closes 1.2 seconds after connecting

requirements.title: A card that has just connected shows a centred success view for the celebration window
requirements.preconditions: The card's id is in the celebrating set.
requirements.expected_result: The header, summary, sample tools, any error line and the corner information button are all replaced by a centred block: a filled check-mark circle glyph at 34 points in the success colour, scaled from 0.5 to 1 with a 0.5-second spring of bounce 0.4 and left at 0.5 when reduce-motion is on, above the line "Connected · " plus the tool count plus " tools" at 12 points medium. The block has a minimum height of 120 and fills the card's width. Note the card, unlike the setup panel, does NOT set the scale to 1 under reduce-motion, so the glyph stays at half size for the whole celebration.
failure_cases: under reduce-motion the celebration never runs at all, because the page's handler returns early
requirements.windows_path: Same view and the same reduce-motion asymmetry with the setup panel; it is unreachable in practice because reduce-motion suppresses the celebration entirely, and is recorded so a port does not diverge if that changes.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test capturing the card during the 900 ms window
